decisions.statement: A statement is read from the file the parser read rather than from the page a loader built.
A decision is judged here and nothing else a page says.
A consequence joined to a fact is refused as a reason is refused.
A statement is refused for the words joining two facts rather than for the two facts.
A mark inside a spelt name is no mark of the statement's own.
A word inside a spelt name is no word of the statement's own.
A statement written in a shape akasha refuses is not plain.
A statement is judged against every refused shape the index names.
A statement already refused for a mark is not judged against the shapes too.
A refusal names the shape that matched.
A statement no refused shape matches is passed over rather than refused.
A sentence no shape reaches is a gap in the shapes rather than a fault in the statement.
Every decision under akasha is plain.
A mark a reason follows is refused as a reason rather than as a join.

definition: the check refusing a decision that is not written in plain language
